title: The arts in transition
summary: Pandora's box is open; persisting with old tools causes harm.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: This is going somewhere and we're certainly in a period of transition, all the arts. If you look at it one way, you're dead, and it just might be dead too, but on the other hand it may not be. It may be something else is forming, it can't possibly be anything that it was because Pandora's Box has been opened and you can't restuff it. But you somehow have to use what's there and that's the lesson of art anyway, it seems to me. And if living is an art, you better pay heed. We could destroy the whole thing, we have it within our means to destroy it, but that doesn't necessarily follow that we will. But it will never be what it was, so you can shed a tear, if that's the way you feel about it. On the other hand, certain things could get better and the only thing, it seems to me that's stopping it, is the unwillingness to recognize what's there and why it's there. A lot of the evils come
from persisting to pursue the present with the tools of the past. If you use that in art you've got a big problem on your hands.
That's the question of defining the tools of the past. It just isn't always apparent what they were.

I think the hardest thing is to maintain a happy medium. There are some people who just, anything new they can't take, because they're listening totally with the sort of ears the acquired from yesterday. But on the other hand, you have people who embrace anything new just because it's new.
Then there is nothing really new, ever. So what is old, is not old; if there's nothing new then it can never be old.
In each case, they're latching onto something that is a fallacy.
